- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid undershooting.  
- If recent 3–5 day price drop is followed by forecast spike, apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 10–15% for the next 3–5 days.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true outcome by > 2% for 3+ consecutive days, apply a “mean reversion” rule — adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- For horizon > 14 days, reduce forecast sensitivity to sentiment — use only 60% of sentiment weight unless sentiment > 0.6.  
- If sentiment is flat (0.0–0.1) and forecast deviates > 3% from true, assume “no sentiment bias” — use historical mean as anchor.
